slot.brief: For a planet, given escape speed, ask for the orbital speed of a satellite close to its surface (or vice versa) using the fixed ratio between them.

stem: A satellite moves in a circular orbit just above the surface of a spherical planet at $8.0\ \text{km s}^{-1}$. What is the escape speed from the planet's surface?

verdicts.working: For a circular orbit just above the surface, the orbital speed is \(v_c=\sqrt{GM/R}=8.0\ \text{km s}^{-1}\). Escape speed is \(v_e=\sqrt{2GM/R}=\sqrt2v_c=8\sqrt2\ \text{km s}^{-1}\).

working:
$v_e=\sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}$, $v_o=\sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{R}}$.
$v_e=\sqrt{2}\,v_o=8\sqrt{2}\ \text{km s}^{-1}$.

Independent check: For a circular orbit just above the surface, the orbital speed is \(v_c=\sqrt{GM/R}=8.0\ \text{km s}^{-1}\). Escape speed is \(v_e=\sqrt{2GM/R}=\sqrt2v_c=8\sqrt2\ \text{km s}^{-1}\).
